definition: Eigen-decomposition is the method of decomposing a square matrix into its eigenvalues and eigenvectors, which is an important tool for simplifying matrix operations and analyzing systems.
details: Eigen-decomposition is the method of decomposing a square matrix into its eigenvalues and eigenvectors, which is an important tool for simplifying matrix operations and analyzing systems.

explainer.lead: Eigen-decomposition rewrites a square matrix using special directions, called eigenvectors, and the amounts by which it stretches them, called eigenvalues. When such a decomposition exists, it can make repeated matrix operations much easier to calculate and understand.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a machine that stretches arrows without turning some of them. Eigen-decomposition finds those special arrows and records how much each one is stretched. Once you know that, using the machine many times is easy: just stretch each special arrow again and again.
tiers.practitioner: For a diagonalizable matrix, form A = V Λ V⁻¹, where V contains eigenvectors and Λ contains eigenvalues on its diagonal. This is useful for matrix powers because Aᵏ = V Λᵏ V⁻¹, but the inverse requires a full set of linearly independent eigenvectors. Do not assume every square matrix can be decomposed this way.
tiers.paperLevel: For a square matrix A, eigen-decomposition expresses it as A = V Λ V⁻¹ when A has n linearly independent eigenvectors; V contains those eigenvectors, and Λ = diag(λ₁, …, λₙ) contains their eigenvalues. Each pair satisfies A vᵢ = λᵢ vᵢ. The method is limited by whether the matrix is diagonalizable.

explainer.example: For A = [[2, 0], [0, 3]], the eigenvalues are 2 and 3, with eigenvectors [1, 0] and [0, 1]. Since A is already diagonal, V is the identity matrix and Λ = A. Therefore A⁵ = [[2⁵, 0], [0, 3⁵]] = [[32, 0], [0, 243]].

usedIn.name: Matrix computation
usedIn.detail: Simplifies calculations such as taking repeated powers of a diagonalizable matrix.

usedIn.name: Systems analysis
usedIn.detail: Represents a square matrix in terms of its eigenvalues and eigenvectors to analyze its behavior.

explainer.intuition: An eigenvector keeps its direction when the matrix acts on it, while its eigenvalue tells how much it is scaled. Eigen-decomposition describes the matrix through these directions and scaling factors instead of its original entries.
howItWorks: Start with a square matrix A.
Find its eigenvalues and corresponding eigenvectors.
Place the eigenvectors as columns of V and the eigenvalues on the diagonal of Λ.
If V is invertible, write A = V Λ V⁻¹.
Use this form to simplify operations such as computing matrix powers.
explainer.whyItMatters: It turns a matrix into a form where its action along independent directions is explicit. This can simplify matrix operations and support analysis of systems represented by matrices.
misconceptions: Not every square matrix has an eigen-decomposition of the form A = V Λ V⁻¹.
Eigenvalues and eigenvectors are not extra matrices added to A; together they provide a way to represent A.
